question: How can the posterior over latent variables and the model evidence be approximated deterministically when exact inference or MCMC is infeasible?
contributions: Variational inference with factorized q (mean field): ln q*_j = E_{i!=j}[ln p(X,Z)] + const (10.9)
Worked variational treatments: univariate Gaussian, Bayesian mixture of Gaussians, linear regression, logistic regression
Local variational bounds via convex duality, including the Gaussian lower bound on the logistic sigmoid
Expectation propagation (minimises KL(p||q) by moment matching), with the clutter problem and its link to loopy belief propagation

limits: No experiments beyond small illustrations (Old Faithful, one synthetic polynomial, one synthetic logistic data set, 1-D clutter); no benchmark numbers for EP vs VB vs Laplace in text (Fig 10.17 axes only).
Factorized KL(q||p) underestimates variance and locks onto one mode (Fig 10.2, 10.3); the author gives no remedy beyond EP.
Local bound for the sigmoid is binary only; the multiclass softmax needs Gibbs (1997), whose Gaussian bound is only conjectured.
EP can fail to converge, and for mixtures its results are 'not sensible'.
Grouping and disconnection choices for EP on graphs are called an open research issue.
2006 text: no stochastic/amortised VI, no reparameterisation gradients, no VAEs or normalising-flow posteriors; dated for modern deep latent-variable models.
practices: Choose the variational family only as rich as tractability allows; there is no over-fitting with flexible q (p. 464).
Work with the form ln q*_j = E_{i!=j}[ln p(X,Z)] + const, then restore normalisation by inspection (p. 466).
Initialise all factors, then cycle through updating each in turn; the bound is convex in each factor (p. 466).
Monitor the lower bound during re-estimation: it must never decrease, which checks derivation and code; finite differences give a deeper check (p. 481).
Use conjugate priors so each optimal factor keeps the prior's functional form (p. 479).
Exploit induced factorizations found by a d-separation test; do not store full matrices that are always diagonal (p. 485).
Pick K by a large initial K with small Dirichlet alpha0 so surplus components shrink, or by maximising the bound w.r.t. pi (ARD pruning) in one run (pp. 480, 484).
When comparing K, add ln K! to the bound (p. 484).
Prefer variational logistic regression over Laplace for accuracy: a rigorous bound is optimised (p. 498).
Optimise xi_n by EM-style update (xi_n)^2 = phi_n^T (S_N + m_N m_N^T) phi_n; typically a few iterations (p. 501).
Use EP rather than ADF in batch settings, since ADF depends on data order (p. 510).

terms.definition: a mapping that takes a function as the input and that returns the value of the functional as the output
ln p(X) = L(q) + KL(q||p) with L(q)=integral q(Z) ln{p(X,Z)/q(Z)} dZ
factorized form of variational inference corresponds to an approximation framework developed in physics
D_alpha(p||q)=4/(1-alpha^2)(1 - integral p^((1+alpha)/2) q^((1-alpha)/2) dx); KL(p||q) is alpha->1, KL(q||p) is alpha->-1; alpha<=-1 zero forcing, alpha>=1 zero avoiding
additional factorizations that arise from an interaction between the factorization assumed in the variational posterior and the conditional independence properties of the true joint distribution
parameters are intensive (fixed in number independent of data set size), latent variables are extensive (scale with data set size)
for conjugate-exponential directed models, q updates are local calculations on the Markov blanket, cast as messages from parents, children and co-parents
g(lambda) = max_x {lambda x - f(x)}; f(x) = max_lambda {lambda x - g(lambda)}
approximate posterior as a product of exponential-family factors, refining each in turn by minimising KL(p||q) via moment matching
setting mean and covariance of q equal to those of p when minimising KL(p||q) within the exponential family (E_q[u]=E_p[u])
EP special case: initialise all factors except the first to unity and make one pass updating each once

code.snippet: ln q*_j(Z_j) = E_{i!=j}[ln p(X, Z)] + const
sigma(x) >= sigma(xi) exp{(x - xi)/2 - lambda(xi)(x^2 - xi^2)}
q^{\j} = q / f_j; set moments of q^new equal to those of q^{\j} f_j, Z_j = integral q^{\j} f_j; f_j = Z_j q^new / q^{\j}; p(D) ~ integral prod f_i
